prompt: Why does the API keep its data in `planner.json` and not in `seed.json`?

choices.text: Node cannot write to a file that git tracks
choices.why: Git does not lock files; Node can write anywhere it may.

choices.text: So the seed stays as it was
choices.why: Right. The working copy is made from the seed when missing.

choices.text: `seed.json` is read-only for the dev server
choices.why: The dev server no longer reads either file.

choices.text: JSON files under `server/` are served to the browser
choices.why: Nothing serves `server/`; the API answers on port 3000.

prompt: `curl -X PATCH .../api/sessions/5 -d '{"done":"yes"}'` was refused. With what?

choices.text: 404, there is no session 5
choices.why: Session 5 exists; the refusal was about the body.

choices.text: 400, done must be true or false
choices.why: Right. `"yes"` is a string, not a boolean.

choices.text: 200, with `done` set to true
choices.why: The server checks the type before it changes anything.

choices.text: 500, because the JSON could not be read
choices.why: The JSON was valid; its value was the wrong type.

prompt: What problem does the dev server's proxy solve?

choices.text: It makes the API answer faster by caching it
choices.why: It passes requests on; it keeps nothing.

choices.text: It lets the API read the application's files
choices.why: The API reads its own two files.

choices.text: The two share one origin, so no CORS needed
choices.why: Right. The browser only ever asks port 4200.

choices.text: It restarts the API when its code changes
choices.why: The API is restarted by hand, in its own terminal.

prompt: After `ng config` set `proxyConfig`, why did the dev server have to be restarted?

choices.text: It reads the proxy when it starts
choices.why: Right. A change to `angular.json` is not watched like the code is.

choices.text: `ng config` stops it on purpose
choices.why: `ng config` only edits `angular.json`.

choices.text: Port 4200 was taken by the API
choices.why: The API listens on 3000.

choices.text: The cache in `.angular` had to be cleared first
choices.why: No cache was involved.

prompt: In Angular 21, what had to be added to `app.config.ts` before the store could `inject(HttpClient)`?

choices.text: `provideHttpClient()`, or the injection fails with `NG0201`
choices.why: That was true before Angular 21; the store worked with no change to the config.

choices.text: Nothing: `HttpClient` already has `providedIn: 'root'`
choices.why: Right. `provideHttpClient()` arrives later, to switch on interceptors.

choices.text: `HttpClientModule` in the component's `imports`
choices.why: That is the module-era way, and nothing here needed it.

choices.text: `withFetch()`, since there is no other way to send a request
choices.why: Without it, requests go through `XMLHttpRequest`.

prompt: What does `HttpClient` do that a plain `fetch` leaves to you? Choose every one.

choices.text: It reads the JSON of the answer
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: It treats a 404 or a 500 as an error
choices.why: Right. `fetch` resolves with any status.

choices.text: It sends every request through the interceptors
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: It checks the answer against the type argument
choices.why: Nothing checks a type argument at run time.

choices.text: It keeps answers so a second request is not sent
choices.why: It sends every request it is asked to.

prompt: For reading, the store uses `___(() => '/api/planner')`, a resource whose loader is an `HttpClient` GET.
The first page that imported `@angular/common/http` connected to the dev server twice. Why?

choices.text: The store sent its GET twice
choices.why: The network list shows one GET.

choices.text: The proxy reconnects on every request
choices.why: The proxy is between the dev server and the API, not the page.

choices.text: A new package was prepared, then the page reloaded
choices.why: Right. It happens once per package.

choices.text: `look` opens every page twice
choices.why: Every other look in the lesson connected once.

prompt: Session 5's minutes became `"50"`, a string. Why did the compiler say nothing?

choices.text: The dev server skips type checking in development
choices.why: It checks types; the data was not code.

choices.text: `httpResource` converts strings to numbers
choices.why: It did not, which is why the total became `11550`.

choices.text: A type argument is a claim, unchecked
choices.why: Right. The compiler believed `minutes: number`.

choices.text: `minutes` was declared as `number | string`
choices.why: `Session` declares it as `number`.

prompt: With session 5's minutes as the string `"50"`, the week said `11550` minutes planned. How many minutes of the week came before session 5 in the sum?
What does `parse: parsePlanner` change about the resource?

choices.text: A bad answer becomes an error, with its message
choices.why: Right. The week said which session and which field.

choices.text: It turns `"50"` into `50`, so the total is right
choices.why: It refuses the answer; it repairs nothing.

choices.text: It makes the request again until the answer passes
choices.why: It runs once per answer.

choices.text: It moves the check to build time
choices.why: The check runs on each answer, at run time.

prompt: A store method calls `this.http.patch(url, body)` and nothing else. What happens?

choices.text: The request is sent and its answer ignored
choices.why: An Observable does nothing until somebody subscribes.

choices.text: No request is sent
choices.why: Right. Nobody subscribed, so nothing ran.

choices.text: The request is sent twice, once per screen
choices.why: There is one store; and no request is sent at all.

choices.text: The compiler refuses an unused Observable
choices.why: It compiles, which is what makes it easy to miss.

prompt: How did the lesson show that the tick reached the server?

choices.text: The checkbox stayed ticked on the same page
choices.why: The page's copy ticks whether or not the server hears.

choices.text: The dev server printed the PATCH
choices.why: The dev server passes requests on and logs only errors.

choices.text: A fresh page loaded 140 minutes done from the API
choices.why: Right. A new page knows only what the server sends it.

choices.text: `git status` listed `planner.json` as changed
choices.why: `planner.json` is ignored by git.

prompt: Changing the copy at once and telling the server afterwards is called an ___ update.
Why did the `GET` from `httpResource` carry the `X-Requested-By` header too?

choices.text: The store added it to the resource's options
choices.why: The store did not change in that section.

choices.text: `httpResource` sends its request through `HttpClient`, and so through the chain
choices.why: Right. One chain for every request.

choices.text: The proxy copies headers from earlier requests
choices.why: The proxy passes on what it receives.

choices.text: The browser adds custom headers to every request on its own
choices.why: The browser adds none of yours.

prompt: Why does an interceptor call `req.clone({ setHeaders: ... })` rather than setting a header on `req`?

choices.text: `clone` sends the request a second time
choices.why: `next` sends it, once.

choices.text: Headers can only be set on a copy of the browser's request
choices.why: The request is Angular's object, not the browser's.

choices.text: An `HttpRequest` cannot be changed, so a changed copy is passed on
choices.why: Right. Immutability keeps each step from surprising the next.

choices.text: `setHeaders` works only during the first request
choices.why: It works on every request.

prompt: Match each interceptor with what it lets an application do.

pairs.left: logs the method, URL and time
tries again on a network failure
pairs.right: survive a moment of bad Wi-Fi

prompt: With the API stopped, the page got a 500. Who sent it?

choices.text: The API, as it shut down
choices.why: Nothing was listening on port 3000.

choices.text: The dev server's proxy
choices.why: Right. Its terminal said `ECONNREFUSED`.

choices.text: The browser, which turns refused connections into 500
choices.why: Without a proxy the browser would report status 0.

choices.text: `httpResource`, after a timeout
choices.why: The status came over the network, from the proxy.

prompt: Before the fix, a failed `PATCH` left the box ticked. What was wrong with that, beyond the console error?

choices.text: The box could not be unticked again
choices.why: It could; the page would just keep lying.

choices.text: The week's total doubled
choices.why: The total moved by 50, as for any tick.

choices.text: The server saved the tick anyway, later
choices.why: The server never received it.

choices.text: The page and the server disagreed
choices.why: Right. A reload would quietly undo it.

prompt: Why does the message go in a paragraph with `role="alert"`?

choices.text: It makes the paragraph red
choices.why: `role` changes what is announced, not how it looks.

choices.text: It stops the box from being ticked again
choices.why: Nothing about the role touches the box.

choices.text: A screen reader announces it at once
choices.why: Right. Somebody who cannot see the box untick hears why.

choices.text: It sends the message to the server's log
choices.why: It is an attribute of the page.

prompt: A request fails with 400 because the body was wrong. What should the application do?

choices.text: Retry it three times, then give up quietly
choices.why: A 400 fails the same way every time, and quiet is the one thing it must not be.

choices.text: Undo what it showed, and show the server's reason
choices.why: Right. The page goes back to what the server believes.

choices.text: Ignore it, since the next request will fix it
choices.why: Nothing will resend this one.

choices.text: Reload the whole page
choices.why: A reload hides the error and loses the reason.
